newsitem.title: USA: Gulfstream hits new high after USAF contract.
newsitem.headline: Gulfstream hits new high after USAF contract.

text.p: Shares of Gulfstream Aerospace Corp jumped to a new high on Monday after the aircraft manufacturer said it won a $68.9 million contract to build two luxury jets to transport top U.S. leaders for the U.S. Air Force, including the President of the United States.
Shares rose 1-1/8 to 26-5/8 and touched a new high of 26-3/4 in intraday trading since their October 1996 initial public offering.
The company said the contract has options for up to four additional jets before 2003, which would bring the total value of to over $275 million. The aircraft are designated C-37A.

Savannah, Georgia-based Gulfstream will build two Gulfstream V aircraft for a program to expand the mission capability of the U.S. Special Air Mission Wing. The jets will be assigned to part of an Air Force command that provides air transportation services for the President of the United States and other national leaders.
Gulfstream will provide technical and logistic support, spare parts and overhaul services to the Air Force for 10 years, it said.
